entry.title: Post Quantum Recovery Framework
entry.summary:
An analysis of unspent transaction outputs (UTXOs) at Bitcoin block 975,019 provides insight into how much BTC is protected by secrets that are either already revealed or remain hidden. Outputs whose public keys are directly present in the output script, or for which a confirmed transaction has disclosed the key or script behind its hash, are considered to have no accidental secret remaining. According to a detailed census, such outputs account for 6,942,209 BTC across 47,351,492 outputs, representing 34.5% of all unspent BTC at this block height. Including Pay-to-Taproot (P2TR) outputs brings this figure to 7,164,754 BTC or 35.6%, though P2TR is categorized separately due to uncertainty about its precise classification within existing frameworks.
The breakdown of output types reveals specific distributions: standard formats such as P2PKH, P2WPKH, P2SH, and P2WSH with their keys or scripts already on chain constitute 5,227,522 BTC, while legacy P2PK outputs account for 1,714,619 BTC. Bare multisig outputs contribute only a negligible amount. The category encompassing outputs where nothing has yet been revealed on chain—specifically, those same four main script types—contains the majority share, totaling 12,941,835 BTC, or 64.4% of all unspent coins. Other forms not classified explicitly represent a minor fraction.
The census methodology does not distinguish outputs based on coin creation time, so it cannot determine how many of the P2PK outputs predate BIP32 nor can it segment coins by era. Additionally, exposure resulting from off-chain disclosure—such as sharing an xpub with a server—or on-chain disclosures outside the scope of census rules, would shift outputs from the “hidden” to the “revealed” category. Determining whether an output retains an essential secret is also impossible through on-chain data alone.
Regarding multisig outputs, the census identifies whether a P2SH or P2WSH script has been revealed but does not analyze the script content, making further classification impossible unless the script is exposed. Available figures indicate 749,474 BTC in P2WSH outputs with on-chain scripts and 371,870 BTC in exposed P2SH outputs that correspond to a revealed script and are distinct from nested-P2WPKH wrappers, as detailed in the [results file](https://github.com/duncan0k/btc-exposure-index/blob/2a0f4b053cad2ae3dc101a4e4c154ac2b4706f25/results/975019/utxo-census-stats.json).
A nuanced question arises regarding the treatment of P2TR outputs. The census treats all 222,545 BTC in 53,016,095 P2TR outputs as exposed because the output key is visible on chain. However, internal keys or script trees, which constitute potential accidental secrets, remain undisclosed until a script-path spend occurs. Further details about the UTXO census methodology, output counts, and exact amounts per type can be found on the [method page](https://snapshots.ark0.si/method.html), and additional discussion is available in the [UTXO census at block 975,019](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/how-much-btc-sits-behind-keys-or-scripts-already-on-chain-block-975-019/3088).
